Row writers (gdn_stats.hpp:203-235, 399-412): only the worker that owns a row writes it. Worker 0 is the forward thread and worker w is pool worker w-1 (TronCpp.hs:1622-1623), so relaxed load-add-store is enough. Rows of two workers never share a cache line (192 bytes per row, 64-byte alignment).

Per-forward stamp slots (gdn_stats.hpp:284-295, 374-379, 418-441): each worker writes only its own lines. The forward thread reads and clears them after the plugin's run has waited for all workers (workers_done.wait, TronCpp.hs:1712). An index error in the slot stride would fail the wall test at t_gdn_stats.cpp:284.
One call per (worker, operation) per forward: validate_recurrent_minibatch asserts exactly one minibatch (model.hpp:2405), so a span slot is written at most once per forward.

Bounds: worker_ix < n_workers = 1 + n_main_helpers <= 1 + pool workers = row count (TronCpp.hs:1684-1689, model.hpp:1755-1756). Operation i has id i < gdn_operations.size() (gdn_registry.hpp:97-98). row(), timers_at() and forward_span() assert all three indexes.
Two model states at once and EAGLE draft states: each state owns its own model_stats, so no row, span or class is shared. The draft publishes under gdn_eagle/ (gdn_stats.hpp:738).

Tokens are counted exactly once per key head on every path: in-place chains in gdn_execution.hpp:179-183, working copies in gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:542-543, never both. run_gdn_operation never calls step() on a working copy. A chain always has at least 1 token (gdn_chain_plan.hpp:135). A refused block is counted once, under amx (see finding 5).
Cycle fields: start, pre, the recurrence per path, post and write are disjoint stamp intervals inside entry..exit, so their sum is at most busy_cycles.

half_full_block_tokens identity: a full window exists exactly when n_tokens >= to_boundary + 32, so every full window is an AMX window when the kernel is available, and a column-half window otherwise (block kernel off, TRON_AMX_GDN_DISABLE, TRON_AMX_DISABLE, no AMX, shape not served). A run with no full window adds 0. Refused blocks stay under amx, so the A/B identity holds.
amx_blocks and amx_fallback_blocks are counted once per value head (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:669-680), as the comment in work_tally says.
No stamp sits inside a per-token loop: 4 stamps per work item (gdn_execution.hpp:148-172) and 4 per window of at most 32 tokens (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:520-547), only when the switch is on.
Off state on the per-call path: one pointer load, one bool, a 136-byte stack tally per run_gdn_operation call, no time stamp, no atomic write, no allocation. forward_scope copies one bool.
GDN wall (gdn_stats.hpp:422-441): the minimum entry and maximum exit over the workers that ran, clamped at 0, filed under the class that forward_scope stored before the workers started.

JSON rendering: key names and commas match the exact-string tests. The largest leaf is 771 bytes with every value at the uint64 maximum (computed with a script), against the limit of 2,048 bytes. An operation with no job renders zeros. The off state renders {} for totals and forwards.

Exit report and lifetime: print_report reads only atomics and constants. The leaf callbacks hold a weak_ptr, so a read after the state is gone returns {}. A later state of the same id replaces the callbacks. Registration before a later constructor failure is safe because the member shared_ptr is released.

forward_scope placement (model.hpp:2161-2168): constructed before any worker starts and destroyed after the attention scope and the latch guard. The forward wall is stamped before the fold. The GDN forward wall includes the attention begin/end bookkeeping when both switches are on. I did not measure that cost.

findings.title: README does not give the unit of amx_blocks or the scope of token_recurrence_cycles, so two obvious checks come out wrong
findings.problem: Lines 340-343 say that amx_blocks counts 'the blocks of block_tokens tokens that the AMX block kernel finished'. The code counts one block per value head (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:669-680), while amx_head_tokens counts once per key head (lines 542-543). Lines 344-347 list 'the three <path>_recurrence_cycles' as like parts. token_recurrence_cycles is the whole step() loop: convolution, recurrence, norm and output gate (gdn_execution.hpp:182, gdn_stats.hpp:193). half_ and amx_recurrence_cycles are the recurrence alone, with the rest in pre_cycles and post_cycles.
findings.scenario: Qwen3.5 4B has 16 key heads and 32 value heads. One full window of one work item adds 32 to amx_head_tokens and 2 to amx_blocks. A reader who checks amx_blocks x block_tokens against amx_head_tokens finds twice the tokens and suspects double counting. A reader who divides each recurrence counter by its head tokens to compare the token path with the chain kernel compares a whole step with a recurrence alone, and overstates the gain of the chain kernel.
findings.fix: Say 'value-head blocks' and give the identity amx_blocks + amx_fallback_blocks = amx_head_tokens / block_tokens x n_value_heads / n_key_heads. Add one sentence that token_recurrence_cycles covers the whole step(), and that the like-for-like value of a working copy is pre + recurrence + post.

findings.title: Comment on BLOCK_TOKENS_32 states the wrong block grid
findings.problem: Lines 134-135 say 'The blocks of a chain are counted from its first token, and that is the grid of half_full_block_tokens'. advance() cuts windows where the position in the sequence reaches a multiple of 32 (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:514-517, Note at lines 104-109), not from the first token of the chain. gdn_stats.hpp was not updated by commit 28c5dda93d.
findings.scenario: A chain of 71 tokens that starts at position 7. The comment predicts two full blocks, 64 tokens per key head. The code gives windows of 25, 32 and 14 tokens, so half_full_block_tokens or amx_head_tokens grows by 32. A reader who predicts the AMX volume from this comment is wrong for every chain that does not start on a multiple of 32, for example after a resume from a stored state.
findings.fix: Reword: 'A block is a full window of advance(): 32 tokens that start where the token position in the sequence is a multiple of 32. That is the grid of half_full_block_tokens.'

findings.title: amx_head_tokens and amx_recurrence_cycles include blocks that the AMX kernel refused, and the comment gives only one of the two refusal reasons
findings.problem: The path of a window is fixed before the kernel runs (lines 539-546). When advance_value_head refuses a value head, gdn_recurrence_chain_head advances it (lines 675-678), but its tokens stay under amx_head_tokens and its time, plus the refused attempt, stays under amx_recurrence_cycles. gdn_stats.hpp:27 says 'The code that advances a token counts it', and README.stats.md:336-337 says the keys count the tokens 'that each path advanced'. gdn_stats.hpp:180-181 says a block is refused 'because a value was not finite'. The kernel also refuses a finite correction of 2^100 or more (amx_gdn_iface.hpp, Note, paragraph Refusal).
findings.scenario: Both value heads of one key head are refused for one window, for example a state that holds an infinity. Then amx_head_tokens grows by 32 and amx_blocks by 0, and amx_recurrence_cycles grows by the chain-kernel time. amx_recurrence_cycles / amx_head_tokens then mixes the two kernels. The reader can see it only through amx_fallback_blocks.
findings.fix: Document it in the Note and the README: amx_head_tokens counts the tokens of full windows given to the block kernel, the refused share is amx_fallback_blocks / (amx_blocks + amx_fallback_blocks), and amx_recurrence_cycles includes the chain-kernel time of refused value heads. Add the second refusal reason to the comment at gdn_stats.hpp:180.

The existing case 'checkpoints preserve its dependency chain' runs step() with working_copy access.

Window grid arithmetic (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:500-517): no finding. to_boundary is 0 on a boundary, a full window exists exactly when n_tokens >= to_boundary + 32, and window_tokens = min(tokens left, 32 - position mod 32). No size_t expression can overflow for real positions.

Aliasing of output rows with input rows: no finding. The plugin passes five distinct indexed_vector buffers (qwen_3p5_4b.hpp:973-977, 1165; decay and update swap between linear_2 and linear_3 per layer, consistent with the matmul names). An output row that exactly aliases its gate row is still safe in advance(): postprocess reads a gate chunk before it stores the same output chunk, and no later token of the window reads an output row. No test covers that alias case, for step() or for advance().
noexcept on advance(): no finding. It allocates nothing, and TRON_ASSERT aborts instead of throwing.

Concepts and ranges (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:47-59, 475-480): no finding at run time. A non-random-access token container is rejected by the constraint. The body also calls std::ranges::size, so a random-access range without a size passes the constraint and fails inside the body; adding std::ranges::sized_range would state the real need.

Fallback after a refused AMX block (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:673-678): no finding on the chain side. gdn_recurrence_chain_head gets the group-local value head and rewrites all output columns of that head, and the AMX kernel restores MXCSR through a scope object before it returns false (amx_gdn.cpp:141-153).

Cost of the new branch in step() on the decode path: no change visible in the existing runs. Base 273.3 tok/s (run q-orig) against 272.1 to 274.9 tok/s (runs q-a, f-a) at 1 user, prompt 1024, in /home/jhan/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/results/gdn-impl-20261121/rt-results.txt. findings.title: advance() references the AMX tile-region functions in builds without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH
findings.problem: Lines 507-510 call amx_attn_h128g4::begin_region() and end_region() outside any #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH. Both functions are defined only in src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp. CMake compiles that file only when the option is ON (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:220-225). Every other AMX reference in this header sits inside the #ifdef (lines 220, 637, 650). The attention call site does the same (self_attention.hpp:1555-1590). Note [AMX attention dispatch] says that with the option off every dispatch block is excluded (amx_attn_iface.hpp:37-39).
findings.scenario: Configure with the option off and without optimization. The presets asan, tsan and coverage in CMakePresets.json do this: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug gives -O0, and the option defaults to OFF. use_block_kernel is a run-time bool, so at -O0 the compiler emits both calls. Every binary that instantiates advance() (t_gated_delta_net, each plugin with GDN operations) then fails to link with an undefined reference to tron::amx_attn_h128g4::begin_region(). Optimized builds link only because the optimizer removes the dead branch. I did not run a build (reader role); this follows from the code and the CMake files.
findings.fix: Put the two statements of lines 505-510 inside #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, as self_attention.hpp does. Keep use_block_kernel defined outside the #ifdef, because block_window still reads it.

findings.title: No test can fail when advance() cuts the windows wrongly or never calls the block kernel
findings.problem: Four facts leave the window grid and the block dispatch of advance() unprotected. (1) With the block kernel off, every cut gives the same bytes, so the byte tests (lines 2755-2776) cannot see the grid. (2) The case 'stays close to step' accepts equal results. So it passes when the block kernel never runs. On a host without AMX it passes with no WARN, unlike t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp:181-182. (3) Its comment (lines 2780-2783) says every run holds at least one full window of 32 tokens. The combination first_position 7, n_tokens 32 covers positions 7 to 38 and holds none. (4) The only executor-level check of the grid counter is half_full_block_tokens == 0 for a 3-token chain (line 2374).
findings.scenario: Three edits keep every test green on every host. Edit A: cut windows from the chain start in gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:516 (use done instead of position). Edit B: make use_block_kernel always false (line 502). Edit C: change gdn_slice_chunks, which turns block_kernel_shape to false without a diagnostic (lines 221-224). After A, the claim of Note [Rolling GatedDeltaNet execution] that windows follow the token position is broken, and resumed prompts give other bytes than the contract says. After B or C, the AMX block kernel is silently off.
findings.fix: In run_chain_case pass a gdn_stats::work_tally to advance() and return it. Check head_tokens[amx_block] + half_full_block_tokens == 32 x key heads x (grid windows inside the run): 2 windows for (0, 71), 1 for (7, 71), 0 for (7, 32). Where amx_gdn_k128v128::available() is true, also require amx_blocks + amx_fallback_blocks == value heads x that number; elsewhere WARN that the block kernel did not run. Correct the comment for the (7, 32) case.

findings.title: gdn_stats.hpp states a block grid that advance() does not use
findings.problem: The comment at lines 134-135 says: 'The blocks of a chain are counted from its first token, and that is the grid of half_full_block_tokens.' advance() counts full windows on the grid of token positions in the sequence (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:500-517). The Note in the executor says the same as the code (lines 104-109).
findings.scenario: Take a chain with source height 7 and 71 tokens. The comment implies 2 full blocks (64 tokens). advance() finds one full window, positions 32 to 63, and counts 32 tokens per key head as half_full_block_tokens or on the amx path. A reader who uses the comment computes a wrong expected AMX share for prompts that resume inside a window.
findings.fix: Reword to: 'A block starts where the token position in the sequence is a multiple of 32; see Note [Rolling GatedDeltaNet execution].' Optionally fill facts.block_tokens in model.hpp from gdn_window_tokens, so that the stats constant and the executor constant cannot diverge.

findings.title: Two executor comments describe only one of the two paths
findings.problem: (1) Lines 422-423 say: 'A working copy holds the slice layout, which only the chain kernel reads.' The AMX block kernel reads and writes the same layout (amx_gdn_iface.hpp:100-102 and 147-149; call at executor lines 671-674). After this change that holds only for step() in place. On a working copy the recurrence reads window.value (a BF16-rounded copy) and writes window.output, and recurrence_output is unused.

checked: Review narration (positron-code-review): no added comment cites a review round, a reviewer label, an issue or a pull request number. The 'Measured on a Xeon 6962P' lines give lasting reasons for bounds.

Formulas of Note [AMX GatedDeltaNet block kernel] against amx_gdn.cpp: g_t, w_tu, r_t, delta_t, o_t and S_B match the coefficient code at lines 387-418 and stages 1 to 4. The bounds 2^-103 (split exact) and 2^105 (stage 4 sum) agree with the split and with the refusal exponent 227. No finding.

findings.title: Stats comment says blocks are counted from the chain's first token; advance() counts them on the sequence-position grid
findings.problem: Lines 134-135 say: 'The blocks of a chain are counted from its first token, and that is the grid of half_full_block_tokens.' The second commit implements another rule. advance() ends a window where the token position in the sequence reaches a multiple of gdn_window_tokens (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:498-516, and Note [Rolling GatedDeltaNet execution] lines 106-109). The grid starts at sequence position 0, not at the chain's first token.
findings.scenario: A chain has source_height 10 and 40 tokens. By the comment it holds one full block, so a reader expects 32 amx head tokens per key head (or 32 half_full_block_tokens without AMX). advance() cuts it into positions 10..31 (22 tokens) and 32..49 (18 tokens). There is no full window, and both counters read 0. A reader who checks the counters against chain lengths concludes that the AMX path lost tokens.

findings.title: Note [Rolling GatedDeltaNet execution] states that step() and advance() give the same bytes, without the condition

findings.scenario: A reader needs to know whether prefill through advance() is bit-identical to a replay with step(). The reader stops at the first paragraph and answers yes. On an AMX host a 64-token prompt chain takes two block windows, and a share of its bf16 outputs differs by one increment.

With the chain kernel it gives the bytes that step() gives for the same tokens; see Note [GatedDeltaNet chain recurrence] in tron/kernels/gated_delta_net.hpp.' The next paragraph then states the exception for the block kernel, as it does now.

findings.title: amx_fallback_blocks comment gives one of the two refusal reasons; README omits the unit of amx_blocks
findings.problem: Lines 180-181 say the kernel refused the blocks 'because a value was not finite'. The kernel also refuses a block whose corrections are finite but reach 2^100 (amx_gdn.cpp:77-79 and 465-470, and the 'Refusal' paragraph of Note [AMX GatedDeltaNet block kernel]). README.stats.md:340-341 says 'amx_blocks counts the blocks of block_tokens tokens'. The code counts one block per value head (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:679-680), while amx_head_tokens counts once per key head.
findings.scenario: A run shows amx_fallback_blocks > 0. The reader searches for a NaN or an infinity in the state and finds none, because the cause was a finite correction of 2^100 or more. Second case: with two value heads per key head (the grouping that t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp:33 names), amx_blocks x block_tokens is twice amx_head_tokens. By the README text the two should be equal, so the reader suspects double counting.

They ran the chain\n// kernel.' README.stats.md:340-342: '`amx_blocks` counts the value-head blocks that the AMX block kernel finished. One value-head block is one value head over `block_tokens` tokens, so a key head with two value heads adds 2 per block. `amx_fallback_blocks` counts the value-head blocks that it refused.'

findings.title: One kernel has two names: 'chain kernel' and 'slice' in the kernels, 'column_half' and 'half' in the stats

(chain path)' assigns that time to the chain kernel only. AMX block windows add their prepare time to pre_cycles too (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:545).

findings.title: GDN code and the 256 x 4 kernels reach into amx_attn_h128g4 for the AMX probe and the tile region
findings.problem: available(), begin_region(), end_region(), TILE_ROWS_16 and TILE_ROW_BYTES_64 are facts of the process and the thread. They live in a namespace named after one attention shape. Before this change only that shape used them. Now the GDN executor (lines 507-510), amx_gdn.cpp (lines 19-20, 133), model.hpp:1738 and the amx_attn_h256g4 namespace (amx_attn_iface.hpp:260-264) import them from amx_attn_h128g4. The reader must open the attention header to learn that the call is independent of the shape and of attention. A fourth kernel family would add one more import from a namespace whose name describes none of its users.

findings.title: gdn_slice_run and key_head_block are the same nine fields with different offset rules, and three sites compute window strides
findings.problem: gdn_slice_run (gated_delta_net.hpp:433-443) and key_head_block (amx_gdn_iface.hpp:131-141) both hold key, query, key_stride, value, output, value_stride, decay, beta, scalar_stride. The meanings differ. In gdn_slice_run, value/output/decay/beta already point at one value head and one slice. In key_head_block they point at the first value head of the key head, and the kernel adds the head. One holds the scaled query, the other the unscaled one. The layout of gdn_recurrence_window (row strides key_width, value_width, n_value_heads) is spelled out at three sites outside the type: gated_delta_net.hpp:579-592, gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:655-667 and t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp:105-117. The stride fields do not name their unit, while amx_attn_iface.hpp uses s_stride_floats and row_stride_floats.
findings.scenario: A reader who knows one struct reads the other and assumes the same base addresses. block.decay[token * block.scalar_stride + value_head] (amx_gdn.cpp:395) and run.decay[token * run.scalar_stride] (gated_delta_net.hpp:471) then look like a bug in one of the two. A change of the window layout (for example one array per token) needs the same edit at three sites, and a missed site reads wrong rows without a compile error.

findings.title: Three call sites pick the kernel set with 'if constexpr (amx_serves_256x4<geometry>)'; the test already has the missing kernel-set type
findings.problem: packed_amx_query (1726-1737), the QK call (1802-1808) and the PV call (1834-1842) each carry the compile-time clause that picks amx_attn_h256g4 or amx_attn_h128g4. amx_q_pack_elems (241-250) is a fourth place that names both shapes. Each pair of branches differs only in the namespace and the name suffix. t_amx_numerics.cpp:45-81 defines the concept that production lacks: shape_128x4 and shape_256x4, each with head_size, q_pack_elems, pack, qk and pv.
findings.scenario: A reader of the dense-page path must compare three pairs of near-identical calls to confirm that only the shape differs. A third shape (for example 128 x 8) needs a new branch at every site, and a missed site compiles: the else branch silently takes the 128 x 4 kernel at the QK and PV sites, where only the pack site asserts amx_serves_128x4.

findings.title: prepare_window_token repeats the first 16 lines of step()
findings.problem: Lines 605-620 (gather the group's channels, convert the decay and update rows to FP32, convolve in place) are a copy of lines 430-445 of step(). The seven-view argument list at 624-632 repeats 457-462. Only the comment differs by one word ('The kernel takes FP32 views' against 'The recurrence kernel takes FP32 views').
findings.scenario: A reader must compare the two blocks line by line to confirm that the in-place path and the working-copy path prepare a token in the same way. A later change to the gather or to the convolution call (for example another history layout) that reaches only one copy makes a one-token chain and a longer chain differ, and no type error reports it.

findings.title: advance() takes nine parameters and six template parameters; five of them are one row set
findings.problem: advance(tokens, first_position, block_kernel, mixed_qkv, output_gate, decay_input, update_input, output, tally). The five row buffers are one concept: the activation rows of the operation, indexed by token job. The generator already names it (GDN.SequenceInputs, ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:3138). decay_rows and update_rows have the same constraint, gdn_activation_rows<token_range, n_value_heads>.
findings.scenario: At the call sites (gdn_execution.hpp:165-167 and four test calls) a reader must count nine positional arguments to match them to names. A call that swaps decay and update compiles, because both satisfy the same concept, and it returns plausible wrong outputs. step() has this hazard already. advance() repeats it with four more arguments around it.

The copies it was reserved for exist now: gdn_state_to_slices and gdn_slices_to_state run inside start_from_checkpoint and write_checkpoint, so their time is already in start_cycles and write_cycles. findings.fix: Delete the field from work_tally, worker_op_row, add(), row_sums::add, put_counts, the Note (line 42), README.stats.md:346 and the two tests (t_gdn_stats.cpp numbers the keys up to base + 15). If the key must stay for a fixed format, replace the comment with the fact: '// Always 0. The state layout copies of a working copy are counted in\n// start_cycles and write_cycles.' and say the same in the README.

findings.title: Comment prose in amx_gdn_iface.hpp: undefined terms, joined claims, one imprecise statement
findings.problem: (a) 'Words used here' (7-13) defines AMX, tile, TDPBF16PS, bf16 and AVX-512. The Note then uses MXCSR, FTZ, DAZ and 'subnormal' (62-70) without a definition. amx_gdn.cpp:136-137 says what the two bits do and does not expand the names. (b) Semicolons join two claims at 9-11, 108, 124-126 and 149-151, and at gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:271-272. (c) 'A value head that forgets fast' (66-67) is a figure of speech. (d) 'An infinity or a NaN in S0 makes every correction non-finite' (75-76) is not exact: only the corrections of the value column that holds the value become non-finite. (e) amx_gdn.cpp:31-33 uses 'pair-interleaved operand' and 'row-major operand' 180 lines before pair_row defines the first term.
findings.scenario: A reader who does not know the x86 control register cannot tell from the Note what 'sets the MXCSR bits FTZ and DAZ' changes. A reader who tests claim (d) with one infinity finds finite corrections in the other 127 columns and doubts the refusal logic, although the lane-wise maximum does catch the one column.
findings.fix: (a) Add to line 13: 'MXCSR is the control register of the SSE and AVX-512 floating-point instructions. Its bit FTZ (flush to zero) makes a subnormal result zero, and its bit DAZ (denormals are zero) makes a subnormal operand count as zero. A subnormal value is a non-zero value below 2^-126, the smallest normal FP32 magnitude.' (b) 9-11: '...into a tile of FP32 values. This text calls one execution a tile product.' 108: 'Probed once. The result is cached for the process lifetime.' 124-126: '...values that are representable in bf16. normalized_query has the same form and carries no query scale. The three strides count floats.' 149-151: 'Returns false when the kernel refuses the block. The matrix is then untouched, and the output columns hold no result.' checked: Block form: derived r_t, delta_t, o_t and S_B from gdn_recurrence (gated_delta_net.hpp:254-305). The Note formulas and the four stages of amx_gdn.cpp match the derivation.

Operand layouts: the A operand is row-major (kq, kt_rows). The B operand is pair-interleaved (kt_pairs, state_pieces, delta_pieces) with lane n = even row in the low 16 bits and odd row in the high 16 bits. This matches the index rule of TDPBF16PS (the AMX bf16 tile product).
Tile loads: every load address and stride (kq 256 bytes, kt_rows 64 bytes, piece tiles 64 bytes) stays inside its array for all loop values.

Tile stores: gh (stride 128 bytes, column 0 or 16), ru (stride 512 bytes, 8 column groups) and update (stride 64 bytes). The last store of each ends exactly at the end of its array. No store runs past a buffer.
transpose_16x16: traced lane by lane through the three shuffle levels. rows[i] holds column i. kt_rows[key][token] = K[token][key].
INTERLEAVE_LOW and INTERLEAVE_HIGH: dst[2j] = even[j] or even[16+j], dst[2j+1] = odd[j] or odd[16+j]. kt_pairs[step][tile][p][2j+e] = K[16*tile+j][32*step+2p+e] as the comment says.

Coefficient tables: w_tu is built by multiplication only. Lane t is set to 1 at token t. Lanes u > t are never read by the triangular loop. decay_to_end holds w_31,u. The own coefficient is scale * (q_t . k_t).
split and pair_row: the three pieces add up exactly for magnitudes of 2^-103 or more. With FTZ set the third piece has no low 16 bits, so the mask in pair_row changes nothing.

Refusal test: the sign bit is masked and the compare is unsigned. So -0.0, negative values, every NaN payload and infinities are handled. An infinity or NaN in S0 always reaches a correction through the second piece.
Stage 4 overflow bound of the Note (below 2^105): holds because every decay is at most 1 (gdn_decay is exp of a value that is not positive). The interface does not state this precondition.

MXCSR scope: flush_subnormals_scope is an RAII object, so the early return restores MXCSR. pack_key_head has no floating-point arithmetic (loads, shifts, permutes, tile products), so it needs no scope. The chain fallback runs after the restore.
Final write: g_31 * S0 + update for 64 key rows per part, at the slice-layout address that gdn_state_to_slices uses.
Scratch layout: the fields sum to 118,144 bytes with no padding, which equals BLOCK_SCRATCH_BYTES_118144. Every field is written before it is read within one block.
Note text: the 2^-103 bound, the switch rules and '5 times slower' (task3-decay-cpu140.txt: 2,959 and 3,239 ns against 587 and 598 ns) match the code and the data. Exceptions are in the findings.

Prototype compare (gdn_kernels.hpp): same arithmetic and indices. Two intended differences: no _mm256_zeroupper (task3-zeroupper-cpu140.txt: 590 to 601 ns with it, 590 to 592 ns without it) and no MXCSR scope in the pack function.

Call site for key_heads_per_group > 1: key offset, first_head offsets of value, output, decay and beta, scalar_stride, head_slices and the value_head passed to gdn_recurrence_chain_head are consistent. Read only; no test runs this case.

Fallback after a refusal: the kernel writes only its scratch and the head's output rows. The chain kernel reads normalized_key, scaled_query, value, decay and beta, which are intact, and it rewrites the output rows.

Tile region: begin_region runs only when the run holds a full window. tron::finally releases it. advance() has no early return after the bracket. A GDN statement runs on main workers outside the attention function, so no region is nested.
available(): a function-local static, so its first call is thread-safe. TRON_AMX_GDN_DISABLE is read before the AMX probe.

CMake: amx_gdn.cpp is compiled only with TRON_AMX_DISPATCH and gets the same AMX flags as amx_attn.cpp. Without the option, block_scratch_type is well-formed and no amx_gdn function is referenced. The amx_attn references are finding 1.

findings.title: The refusal for a non-finite output is not exercised
findings.problem: The refusal test has two arms: a correction of 2^100 or more (line 465) and a non-finite output (line 467). All three refusal sections of t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp (infinity, NaN, value 3e38) trip the first arm, because a non-finite or huge start value makes the correction non-finite or huge. If the second arm is deleted, every test still passes. The design names this case: the block form can overflow where the token form does not (design.txt section 5.4). The two sections on the bound also leave it open: one correction is at most 0.95 * 2^99, the other at least 0.05 * 3e38 (about 2^123.5), so any bound between 2^99 and 2^123 passes both.
findings.scenario: Every key has 0.0 at coordinates 5 and 6, every query has 0.75 there, and the start matrix has 3e38 at rows 5 and 6 of one column. K S0 does not see these rows, so all corrections stay small. Q S0 is 0.75 * 3e38 * 2 = 4.5e38, which overflows FP32 in the tile sum, so the output is infinite. The token form scales the query first and gives a finite output of about 4e37. Without the second arm the kernel accepts the block and returns infinite outputs.
findings.fix: Add a section with these inputs: require that the head is refused and its matrix unchanged. To fix the bound, add a case with a zero start matrix, beta 1.0 at token 0 and a value of exactly 2^100 (refused) and of the next lower bf16 value (taken).

findings.title: No test checks that advance_value_head restores MXCSR
findings.problem: advance_value_head sets the FTZ and DAZ bits of MXCSR (the control register of the vector floating-point unit) and the note promises that it restores the caller's value before it returns, also on the refusal path (amx_gdn_iface.hpp:62-65). No test reads MXCSR after a call.
findings.scenario: A later change replaces the scope object by an explicit set and restore and misses the early 'return false' at line 469. After the first refused block, the worker thread keeps FTZ and DAZ. The chain kernel and step() on that thread then flush subnormal values, so they no longer give the bytes of gdn_recurrence when decay products underflow. Every test passes, because the step() reference runs before advance() and no later case has subnormal values.
findings.fix: In both cases of t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp, read _mm_getcsr() before the kernel calls and require the same value after a block that was taken and after a block that was refused.

findings.title: The chain kernel is never run with more than one key head per group and more than one token
findings.problem: Every advance() call in the tests uses gdn_rolling_head_executor, which has one key head per group. The window's key width then equals key_head_dim. The tests that call step() on a working copy of the whole executor (two key heads) run the chain kernel with one token per window, so the token stride is never applied. Production uses head executors only, so this is a latent path of the template.
findings.scenario: '.key_stride = key_head_dim' in place of window_type::key_width at line 584, or at gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:660, passes every test. The same holds for the key-head loop in advance_window_with_block_kernel and for 'key_heads_per_group * window_tokens' in the tally (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:542).
findings.fix: In run_chain_case, run advance() once more on gdn_rolling_executor<geometry, geometry.n_key_heads> with a working copy (one group, two key heads) and require the same bytes as step().

findings.title: advance() calls the AMX tile-region functions outside #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH
findings.problem: Check: tron-code-review, feature disabled. Lines 507 and 509 call amx_attn_h128g4::begin_region() and end_region() behind the run-time bool use_block_kernel. AMX is Intel's tile-matrix instruction set. Both functions are defined only in src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp. That file is compiled only when the CMake option TRON_AMX_DISPATCH is ON (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:220-221). Without the option, the calls disappear only if the optimizer folds block_kernel_available() to false. self_attention.hpp:1556-1590 keeps the same two calls inside the #ifdef, and Note [AMX attention dispatch] item 1 says every dispatch block is excluded.
findings.scenario: The presets asan, tsan and coverage use CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug (CMakePresets.json:90, 103, 115). Debug is -O0 (CMakeLists.txt:78), and these presets leave TRON_AMX_DISPATCH OFF. At -O0 the compiler keeps both calls. Every binary that instantiates advance() then fails to link with an undefined reference to tron::amx_attn_h128g4::begin_region(). That covers t_gated_delta_net and the Qwen3.5 plugin. Evidence: inspection only, nothing was compiled.
findings.fix: Put lines 505-510 inside #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH and if constexpr (block_kernel_shape), as advance_window_with_block_kernel does at lines 650-651. Make use_block_kernel a constant false in every other build.

findings.title: copy_cycles is rendered in every leaf but nothing writes it
findings.problem: Checks: tron-code-review counter semantics (missing collection read as no work), folks 14 (no writer). work_tally::copy_cycles is 'reserved for state layout copies of the chain path'. No line in h/ or src/ adds to it. README.stats.md:346 lists it as a part of busy_cycles. The layout copies exist: gdn_state_to_slices runs in start_from_checkpoint and gdn_slices_to_state runs in write_checkpoint. findings.title: step() gained a test-only working-copy branch on the decode per-token path
findings.problem: Checks: folks 30 (hot path), folks 14 (no production consumer), folks 18 (duplicated logic). run_gdn_operation sends every working copy to advance() (gdn_execution.hpp:160-168). So the new branch at lines 421-428 is reached only by tests. It sits at the top of step(), the function that runs once per token and key head in decode. If inlined, it pulls the chain kernel into step(). gated_delta_net.hpp:116-118 records that a larger step() once stopped clang from inlining it into the replay loop, and the replay ran slower. prepare_window_token (lines 605-620) is also a verbatim copy of the first 16 lines of the in-place body (lines 430-445).
findings.scenario: Decode with 1-token chains: step() may no longer be inlined into the loop of run_gdn_operation, so every decode token pays a call and loses cross-call optimization. Insufficient data: the decode speed of the base build against this head on delphi-3b35 resolves it. The reader report gdnpath.facts.md:56 asks for the same measurement.
findings.fix: Move the working-copy body into a private TRON(noinline) member, or delete it and let the tests call advance() with one token. Share the gather-and-convolve lines between step() and prepare_window_token through one helper. Report decode tokens per second for base and head.

findings.title: No test proves that advance() takes the block kernel, counts it, or falls back after a refusal
findings.problem: Checks: tron-code-review meaningful tests (deliberate break), folks 33 and 3A. 'GatedDeltaNet advance with the block kernel stays close to step' is the only test that reaches advance_window_with_block_kernel. Its bounds allow exact equality, and it passes no tally. On a host without AMX it passes with no SKIP and no WARN. The counters amx_head_tokens, amx_blocks, amx_fallback_blocks and half_full_block_tokens are asserted only as zero (lines 2371-2374). No test sends a refusing input through the executor.
findings.scenario: Three breaks that fail no assertion on any host. (1) Force block_window to false at gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:518: advance equals step, the test passes, and only speed is lost. (2) Delete the gdn_recurrence_chain_head call at lines 675-678: a refused value head keeps a stale matrix and unfinished outputs. (3) Swap the two counters at line 680, or drop line 544.
findings.fix: In this test pass a work_tally to advance(). When amx_gdn_k128v128::available() is true, require amx_blocks == full windows x value heads and at least one output word that differs from step(). Otherwise require half_full_block_tokens == 32 x full windows x key heads. Add one case that starts from a checkpoint with an infinity in one value head: require amx_fallback_blocks > 0 and the bytes of step() for that head.

findings.title: Block kernel tests run only on AMX hosts, the split rule has no test, and one comment names the wrong input family
findings.problem: Checks: tron-code-review hardware gate and exit code, folks 3A, folks 17. Both test cases do WARN and return when available() is false (lines 181-184 and 284-287). Catch2 counts that as a pass. The split of an FP32 value into three bf16 pieces is plain AVX-512 code, but it sits in the anonymous namespace of amx_gdn.cpp, so only these gated cases reach it. Design section 5.6 lists a split-rule test (exact sum from 2^-103 up, the stated loss below). No such test exists. Lines 188-189 say the 'small values' family takes values below 2^-103. Its scale is 1e-20, about 2^-66, so its three pieces are all normal bf16 values and nothing is dropped.
findings.scenario: On a runner without AMX the binary returns 0 and the lane shows a pass, while no line of the block kernel ran. A change to split() that loses precision only below 2^-103, or only near the largest FP32 value, fails no assertion on any host: no family holds such start values.
findings.fix: Move split() and pair_row() to a header that needs no AMX flags and test them on every host: sum of pieces == value for magnitudes from 2^-103 to the largest FP32 value, and the documented loss below. Use SKIP() in place of WARN plus return, so that a run without AMX shows as skipped. Correct the comment: the decay-underflow family is the one that produces values below 2^-103.

findings.title: At head size 256 the dense AMX page path fills and copies 4,096 bytes per page visit on unchanged lines
findings.problem: Checks: tron-code-review raised size parameter, folks 30 raised-size trigger. The change raises the head size on apply_dense_amx_page from 128 to 256. Line 1847 declares tensor<operation_head_size> scratch with the zero-filling default constructor (tensor.hpp:41-42). Lines 1848-1849 then overwrite all of it with memcpy from amx_o. scratch is only read afterwards, by fma or by v_star.set.
findings.scenario: Per query token, full page and KV head: 4 heads x 1,024 bytes = 4,096 bytes copied at head size 256, against 2,048 bytes at 128. The same number of bytes is zero-filled first in the source. The compiler may remove that fill, because the overwrite is visible in the same function. Not measured, and the object code was not inspected.
findings.fix: Declare tensor<operation_head_size> scratch{uninitialized}. Better: read row `offset` of amx_o through a view in the fma and drop the copy. amx_o is alignas(64) and each row starts at a multiple of 64 bytes. Line 1795 (s_pages, 1,024 bytes zero-filled before the QK kernel writes all of it) does not grow with the head size and can take the same {uninitialized} form.

findings.title: The stats header repeats kernel facts: a false grid comment, a third constant for 32, and a second AMX gate
findings.problem: Checks: folks 17 (comment against code), 18 (duplicate), 31 (one gate per subsystem). Lines 134-135 say the blocks of a chain are counted from its first token and that this is the grid of half_full_block_tokens. advance() counts full windows on the grid of the sequence position (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:514-517). gdn_stats::BLOCK_TOKENS_32 is a third copy of gdn_window_tokens and amx_gdn_k128v128::BLOCK_TOKENS_32, and nothing ties it to them. model.hpp:1742-1745 sets facts.amx_gdn_enabled from shape_ok of kernel 0 only. The executor gate block_kernel_shape (lines 221-224) has two more conditions and is evaluated per kernel.

If gdn_window_tokens changes, the summary key block_tokens still reads 32. If the two gates disagree, the summary reads amx_gdn_enabled true while no window takes the block kernel.

findings.title: amx_head_tokens and amx_recurrence_cycles include refused blocks, and README gives amx_blocks no unit

Its tokens and its time still count as amx. gdn_stats.hpp:27 says 'the code that advances a token counts it', and README.stats.md:336-339 says the keys count the tokens that each path advanced. findings.title: The off-state contract says 'one bool per call and nothing else', but the code does more

findings.title: The 256 x 4 query pack runs before the dense-page test and moves one bf16 pair per iteration
findings.problem: Checks: tron-code-review (work before its test, scalar loop in a vector kernel), folks 30. packed_amx_query (self_attention.hpp:1659-1663) packs a token's query group at its first visible page of the call, before is_dense_amx_page decides whether any page takes the kernels. pack_q_group_256x4 is a triple loop of 512 iterations that moves 2 bf16 values each. The 128 version has 256 iterations.
findings.scenario: A call in which no page of the token is dense, such as decode on a context below 64 tokens or a section of partial pages, writes 2,048 bytes for nothing, twice the 128 cost. Hypothesis, not measured: for a worker section with one full page per token the pack is a visible share of the page unit. An instruction count of the function with the project compiler, and one timed call on the Xeon 6962P, confirm or reject it.
findings.fix: Measure first. If it shows, pack inside the dense branch (apply_page_tok, after is_dense_amx_page) and write the pack with AVX-512 permutes.

findings.title: The stats call the chain kernel 'column-half' and publish 'half' in the JSON keys

findings.fix: Rename the enumerator to chain and the key prefix to 'chain' (chain_head_tokens, chain_recurrence_cycles, chain_full_block_tokens), or name the kernel 'column-half' in gated_delta_net.hpp. Use one name in both commits.
